Title: Justicia
Comment: CRANK IT UP! NYT: “ The title track to his 1969 experimental Latin/R&B fusion album, “Justicia” (“Justice”) sets the standard for salsa’s emblematic focus on socially conscious lyrics. Quintana’s plaintive vocals set off a firestorm of a chorus section, with Palmieri battling with percussion and trombones. The song is a fitting soundtrack for the encroaching 1970s, where Nuyorican urban politics became inseparable from a rumba dance session.”

Title: Medley: Mystery Train / Tiger Man - Midnight Show - Live at the International Hotel, Las Vegas, NV - August 1969
Comment:
[This live performance was first released in November 1969 on From Memphis to Vegas/From Vegas to Memphis]

Elvis played a four week residency in Las Vegas in 1969 when he was at the absolute peak of his "comeback" powers. If you haven't heard the 7:45 version of Suspicious Minds from this album, take a listen!

His TCB (⚡) Band was led by guitarist James Burton, who was inducted into the R&R Hall of Fame by longtime fan Keith Richards in 2001. On bass is Jerry Scheff who played bass on The Doors' "LA Woman" album. The drummer is Ronnie Tutt, who went on to play drums for Billy Joel (Piano Man), the Jerry Garcia Band, Bonnie & Delaney, and both Gram Parsons solo albums.

p.s., Elvis's backing singers for his live performances were The Sweet Inspirations, not heard on this track but heard on the rest of the album, provided backing vocals for all of Aretha's albums from 1967-72, Hendrix's "Burning of the Midnight Lamp" (1968), and The James Gang's "Thirds" (1972)
